title: A crow taught him what his own heart could not.
subtitle: Regret arrives after the deed, holding a shovel

row.title: his brother's body
sub: and no idea what to do

then: This closes the story of Adam's two sons. After the killing, Allah sent a crow scratching the ground to show him {idea}how to cover his brother's body.{/idea} He cried: {trap}woe to me, could I not even be like this crow?{/trap} He became one of the regretful.
now: The angry text you sent at midnight. The words you said to your mother in a fight. {trap}A minute later you are staring at what you did, not knowing how to fix it.{/trap} {idea}Regret is a sign to turn back, while turning back still helps.{/idea}
old: I will deal with the consequences later. Right now I just want to act.
new: Regret after a wrong comes fast and heavy, so I pause before the deed.
try: Before the next angry reply today, picture yourself one hour later. Then decide.

title: Save one life and it is as if you saved everyone.
subtitle: Why one human life weighs as much as all of humanity
then: Because of what Adam's son did, this rule was given. Ibn Kathir says it is so {idea}because there is no difference between one life and another.{/idea} Ibn Abbas explained that saving a life includes {reward}refusing to take a life Allah made sacred.{/reward} Then all people are safe from you.
now: You give blood once a year. You stop to help a stranger who collapsed on the platform. You talk a friend through the worst night of their life. {reward}By this verse, that is everyone.{/reward}
old: Helping one person barely makes a difference in a world this big.
new: One life saved carries the weight of all lives, because each one is sacred.
try: Do one thing today that protects a life: check on someone struggling, or sign up to donate blood.

title: Spreading terror on the land is among the gravest crimes.
subtitle: How seriously Allah treats people's safety
then: Right after the verse about one life, this verse names {trap}very severe penalties{/trap} for those who oppose Allah and spread corruption. Ibn Kathir says this includes {trap}blocking roads and spreading fear{/trap}. Mischief in the land, he says, covers many kinds of evil.
now: You are not a criminal. But you can still make a place feel unsafe: the office bully, the neighbor who scares children, the driver who terrorizes the road. {idea}The verse shows how much Allah values people feeling safe.{/idea}
old: Making people afraid is not a serious sin if no one gets hurt.
new: People's safety is so sacred to Allah that spreading fear is among the gravest wrongs.
try: Notice one place where people feel uneasy around you. Do one thing today to make them feel safe.

title: Even here, the door of return is open.
subtitle: Mercy right after the hardest verse
then: Directly after the most severe penalty, the verse opens an exception: {idea}those who return in repentance before they are caught.{/idea} It ends: {reward}know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.{/reward} Even at the edge, the door is shown.
now: You have a habit no one knows about yet. No one has caught you. {idea}This is the best time to stop: before anyone forces you.{/idea} The verse says turning back by choice is met with {reward}forgiveness and mercy.{/reward}
old: I will stop when I get caught or when things fall apart.
new: Coming back before anyone forces me is the return Allah honors.
try: Name one hidden habit you want to leave. Make a sincere intention today, before anything forces you.

title: Seek the means to come near Him.
subtitle: Mindfulness, a path toward Him, and steady effort
then: Ibn Abbas said wasilah means {idea}the means of approach.{/idea} Qatadah said: {idea}come near Him by obeying Him and doing what pleases Him.{/idea} Wasilah is also the highest rank in Paradise, and the Prophet ﷺ taught that whoever asks for it for him after the call to prayer {reward}will have his intercession.{/reward}
now: The adhan goes off on your phone. Usually you swipe it away. {idea}There is a short dua for that exact moment{/idea}, asking for the wasilah for the Prophet ﷺ. A thirty-second habit that brings you near.
old: Getting close to Allah needs something big that I am not ready for.
new: Every act that pleases Him is a step closer, even a short dua after the adhan.
try: After the next adhan, repeat its words and ask Allah to grant the Prophet ﷺ the wasilah.

title: The whole earth, twice over, would not buy a way out.
subtitle: On that Day, nothing works as ransom
then: Ibn Kathir cites a hadith: a man of the Fire is asked if he would ransom himself with the earth's fill of gold. He says yes. He is told: {trap}you lie, I asked you for less than that and you did not do it.{/trap} {idea}What was asked was small, and asked in time.{/idea}
now: You would give anything to undo a mistake once it is too late. Right now, {idea}what is asked of you is small{/idea}: a prayer, a kind word, a debt repaid. {trap}The price only grows when it is postponed.{/trap}
old: If I ever need to fix things with Allah, I will find a way then.
new: What He asks now is small, and later even the whole earth would not be enough.
try: Do one small act of obedience you have been delaying, today, while it is still small.

title: They will wish to leave, and there will be no exit.
subtitle: Why the time to leave the road is now
then: This verse follows the failed ransom of verse 36. Ibn Kathir explains that they will {trap}long to leave, but have no way of escaping.{/trap} The verse is stated plainly, so that {idea}the door is used while it is still open.{/idea}
now: You are not there. You are here, with a phone in your hand and a whole day ahead. {idea}Every exit from a wrong road is still open to you.{/idea} The verse is a mercy because it tells you this before the doors close.
old: Thinking about the end is depressing, so I avoid it.
new: Hearing about the end now is a mercy, because now I can still choose.
try: Ask Allah today, in your own words, to keep you far from the Fire and to make you leave every wrong road.

title: Taking what is not yours is a serious matter to Allah.
subtitle: A severe penalty, applied the same to everyone
then: Ibn Kathir notes that Islam set {idea}several conditions before this penalty could ever apply.{/idea} When a woman from a noble clan stole and people tried to intercede, the Prophet ﷺ said: those before you were destroyed because {trap}they excused the powerful and punished the weak.{/trap}
now: Office supplies taken home. A borrowed book never returned. The streaming account you were never meant to use. {trap}It feels too small to count.{/trap} {idea}This verse shows how serious Allah is about what belongs to others.{/idea}
old: Small things taken from big companies or rich people do not really count.
new: What belongs to others is a trust, and taking it matters to Allah, big or small.
try: Return one thing today that is not yours, or pay back something you owe, however small.

title: Repent and set things right, and He turns to you.
subtitle: No wrong is so heavy that the door closes

row.title: a clean start
sub: as on the day you were born

then: A woman who stole asked the Prophet ﷺ if she could still repent. He said: {reward}yes, today you are free of your sin as on the day your mother gave birth to you.{/reward} A'ishah said {idea}her repentance was sincere{/idea}, she married, and she used to visit her.
now: Your family still brings up what you did years ago. Your own mind replays it at night. {trap}You feel labeled for life.{/trap} The verse says {reward}Allah turns to the one who repents and reforms.{/reward} His view of you can be new today.
old: After what I did, I will always be that person.
new: Real repentance and a changed life can give me a clean start with Allah.
try: Turn one old regret into a quiet repentance today, and do one good deed that sets part of it right.

title: The heavens and the earth are His. So is the final word.
subtitle: Forgiveness and punishment rest with the Owner of all
then: This verse closes the passage on penalty and repentance. Ibn Kathir says Allah {idea}owns everything and decides what He wills, and no one can resist His judgment.{/idea} After the open door of verse 39, it reminds who {reward}holds the keys to forgiveness.{/reward}
now: People online have already judged you. Your old friends have made up their minds. {trap}Their verdict feels final.{/trap} {idea}It is not.{/idea} The only judgment that lasts belongs to the One who owns the heavens and the earth.
old: Once people have judged me, my case is closed.
new: Only Allah's judgment is final, and His forgiveness is in His hands, not theirs.
try: When someone's harsh opinion of you comes to mind today, turn it into a dua for Allah's forgiveness.
